simple.meaning: נְוָלוּ (nᵉvâlûw) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a sink.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across Ezra, Daniel, beginning at Ezra 6:11. Its contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נְוָלוּ (H5122).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: נְוָלוּ (nᵉvâlûw) / H5122 is traced through Ezra 6:11, Daniel 2:5, Daniel 3:29 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: I have also made a decree that whoever alters this message, let a beam be pulled out from his house, and let him be lifted up and fastened on it; and let his house be made a dunghill for this.

timeline.evidenceText: I have also made a decree that whoever alters this message, let a beam be pulled out from his house, and let him be lifted up and fastened on it; and let his house be made a dunghill for this.
The king answered the Chaldeans, “The thing has gone from me. If you don’t make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you will be cut in pieces, and your houses will be made a dunghill.

Therefore I make a decree, that every people, nation, and language, which speak anything evil against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, shall be cut in pieces, and their houses shall be made a dunghill; because there is no other god who is able to deliver like this.”

definitions.full: H5122. nevalu or nevali נְוָלִר נְוָלוּ, (K § 61, 4. 5 ) noun feminine refuse-heap ( נְוָלִי ᵑ7 dung-heap ; perhaps loan-word from Assyrian namâlu ( nawâlu ), ruin , Jen KB vi. 363 ); — נְוָלוּ Ezra 6:11 , נְוָלִי Dan 2:5 ; 3:29 .
definitions.rootNote: (Aramaic) or נְוָלִי ; (Aramaic), from an unused root probably meaning to be foul;
